accepted.title: Bounded-gap AI re-disclosure during a continuing interaction (companion chatbot laws, 2026)
accepted.nl_spec: The chatbot must say it is artificial and not human at the start of the interaction, and then again at least every three hours (every hour for known minors) while the interaction continues.
accepted.quote: The notification described in subsection (1) of this section must be provided: (a) At the beginning of the interaction; and (b) At least every three hours during continued interaction.
accepted.operational_context: Binding on every operator of an AI companion chatbot serving Washington users (HB 2225, signed 2026-03-24, effective 2027-01-01, private right of action). For known minors, Sec. 4(2)(b) shortens the interval to 'At least every hour during continuous interaction.' The same shape is enacted in Georgia SB 540 (Act 518, 2026; text as passed: '(A) At the beginning of each interaction or session; and (B) At least every three hours during continued interaction', with every hour for minors, https://www.legis.ga.gov/api/legislation/document/20252026/248169) and in New York GBL s.1702 ('at the beginning of any AI companion interaction which need not exceed once per day and at least every three hours for continuing AI companion interactions', https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/1702). China's anthropomorphic-AI measures (CAC Order 21, in force 2026-07-15, Art. 18) add a periodic wall-clock variant: '对用户连续使用拟人化互动服务每超过2个小时的，应当以对话或者弹窗等方式提醒用户注意使用时长' (https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12806/202606/content_7072472.html). If violated, the user loses track of talking to a machine during the long, emotionally intense sessions the laws target. The result is liability under state consumer-protection law, and in Washington private suits.

atoms.name: d
atoms.meaning: the reply discloses that the chatbot is artificially generated and not human

accepted.ltl: Real-time: d at round 1, and for every round i with timestamp t_i, some round j>=i with t_j <= t_i + 3h has d, unless the interaction ends first (equivalently, no gap between consecutive d longer than 3h). Closest turn-count analogue, k=3: d & G(d -> (N d | (N N d) | (N N N d)))
accepted.plain_meaning: The turn version says: disclosure in reply 1, and after every disclosure another one comes within the next three replies, unless the conversation ends first. In the real-time version the bound is three hours of wall-clock time, not three replies.
accepted.checker_output: Turn analogue: VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Closest single instance: 149  AT MOST 4 TIMES, !d GLOBALLY; separating trace {} {} {} {} {d} {} {d} ... (spec false, every implied grammar instance true).
accepted.why_new: Closest grammar spec is EVERY k (exact period). This law sets an upper bound on the gap between disclosures, not an exact period: extra disclosures are allowed and the requirement is measured in hours. The 'at-least-every-k' shape is already a known near miss of EVERY, citing SB 243 for minors. New here: three more binding laws (WA, GA, NY) apply it to all users, two of them with a one-hour minor variant. China Art. 18 gives an exact wall-clock period, whose turn analogue is EVERY k and so is covered. That part is real-time only.

verification.source_and_quote: Fetched the WA legislature XML (Engrossed Substitute HB 2225, certified as passed by both chambers, header "Passed Legislature"). Sec. 3(2) reads "(a) At the beginning of the interaction; and (b) At least every three hours during continued interaction." Sec. 4(2)(b) reads "At least every hour during continuous interaction." for known minors. The fetch tool paraphrased the lead-in "The notification described in subsection (1)...", so I did not confirm that sentence verbatim, but the operative (a) and (b) clauses match. The GA, NY and China quotes in the context field were not fetched by me. They are corroborating extras and do not carry the candidate.
verification.operational: True. The bill was signed by Gov. Ferguson on 2026-03-24 and takes effect 2027-01-01 (Sec. 9). Violations are unfair or deceptive acts under the Consumer Protection Act (Sec. 6). Law-firm summaries report a private right of action, which is available under the CPA, although the bill text does not state it expressly. source_type "law" is correct. It is enacted, not a bill, and binds operators of AI companion chatbots. The safety purpose (users losing track of talking to a machine) matches the stated aim of the statute.
verification.formalization: One atom d on side A (the reply discloses the chatbot is artificial and not human) is a per-round property of the reply and uses no history. The turn formula is d & G(d -> (N d | N N d | N N N d)). It requires d in reply 1. After every d, another d must come within 3 replies unless the trace ends (weak next). That is the same as "d first, and no gap between consecutive d longer than 3 rounds". Hand traces: (1) d . . d . . d is accepted. (2) d . . . d (a 4-round gap) is rejected. (3) d . . with the trace ending is accepted, which matches "unless the interaction ends first". Extra disclosures are allowed, as the statute says "at least". The turn version is only an analogue, because the statute counts hours, not replies. The real-time version needs timestamps. A per-round propositional encoding of a 3-hour bound is not faithful, so the turn analogue is a proxy only. The minor variant (every hour) is the same shape with a smaller bound.
verification.coverage: I ran the checker on the turn analogue: python3 -I covered.py --atoms "d:A" --ltl "d & G(d -> (N d | N N d | N N N d))". VERDICT: NOT COVERED. 54 grammar instances were tried and 1 is implied by the spec. The surviving separating traces include {} {} {} {} {d} {} {d} ..., where the spec is false but every implied grammar instance holds. The closest instance is "AT MOST 4 TIMES, !d GLOBALLY" and it disagrees on a sample of 1516 traces. It is not COVERED and not TRIVIAL. The shape is the bounded-gap "at-least-every-k" pattern, which real-world-examples.md already lists as a known near miss to EVERY k. The new part is that it appears in an enacted binding law with an hourly minor variant.
verification.reasons: The source is a signed, binding statute with a verbatim operative quote, and its safety rationale is real. The turn analogue is NOT COVERED by my own checker run, and the REAL_TIME flag is honest because the per-round encoding is only a proxy. The pattern was already a known near miss, so the contribution is operational weight (enacted laws in WA, with GA, NY and CA SB 243 reported as same-shape), not a new formal shape. Minor caveats: the private right of action is inferred from the CPA, and the lead-in sentence of the quote was not confirmed verbatim.

accepted.title: Disclaimer at the start and at the end of an AI voice interaction (California AB 3030)
accepted.nl_spec: When generative AI produces spoken patient communications about clinical information, the AI disclaimer must be given at the start of the interaction and again at its end.
accepted.quote: (C)For audio communications, the disclaimer shall be provided verbally at the start and the end of the interaction.
accepted.operational_context: California Health & Safety Code s.1339.75 (AB 3030), in force since 2025-01-01. It binds health facilities, clinics and physician offices that use generative AI for patient communications about clinical information, including AI phone and voice agents, unless a licensed provider reviews the communication first. Violations are subject to the Medical Board and facility licensing enforcement. The same section sets ALWAYS for chat ('prominently displayed throughout the interaction'). The audio rule is the only one with an end-of-interaction obligation. The quote is from the statute text reprinted on the page cited (the leginfo page returned 403).

atoms.name: d
atoms.meaning: the agent's turn verbally states that the communication is generated by generative AI

accepted.plain_meaning: The disclaimer is in the first reply and in the last reply of the conversation. Replies in between are unconstrained.
accepted.checker_output: VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Closest single instance: 243  AT MOST 3 TIMES, !d GLOBALLY; separating trace {d} {} {} {} {} {d} {d} {d} {} {} {d} {} {d} {d}.
accepted.why_new: Closest grammar specs are AT 1 and EVENTUALLY. The grammar has no way to refer to the last round. 'At the end of each conversation' already appears as a near miss of EVENTUALLY (a star-rating request), but this is a binding health-care statute. Caveat for the verifier: if 'end' is read as 'in the agent's sign-off turn' (an A atom c), the formula becomes G(c -> d) = ALWAYS(!c | d), which IS covered. The faithful reading of the statute is the end of the interaction, i.e. the last round.

verification.source_and_quote: Fetched the physicianspractice.com page. The quote appears verbatim as subsection (C) of the AB 3030 disclaimer text: "For audio communications, the disclaimer shall be provided verbally at the start and the end of the interaction." The page says AB 3030 was signed in late September 2024 with a compliance date of 2025-01-01.
verification.operational: True. This is an enacted California statute (AB 3030, Health & Safety Code s.1339.75). It binds health facilities, clinics, physician offices and group practices that use generative AI for patient communications about clinical information. Administrative matters such as scheduling and billing are excluded, and so are communications a licensed provider reads and reviews. The page does not itself confirm enforcement details, but the claim does not need them. source_type "law" is correct.
verification.formalization: Atom d is on side A and is a property of one reply (it says the reply verbally states the communication is AI-generated). It contains no history. The formula is d & F(d & !(X true)). Under LTLf strong next, X true is false at the last position, so !(X true) means "last round". The formula therefore requires d in round 1 and d in the last round. Traces I checked by hand: (1) {d}{}{d} satisfies the formula, which is correct. (2) {d}{}{} fails, because no disclaimer at the end. (3) {}{}{d} fails, because no disclaimer at the start. (4) A length-1 trace {d} satisfies it, which is a reasonable reading. This matches "at the start and the end of the interaction" with nothing stronger or weaker. The candidate's caveat is right: the sign-off-turn reading would be covered, but the statute says end of the interaction, so the last-round reading is the faithful one.
verification.coverage: I ran the checker on "d & F(d & !(X true))" with atom d:A. VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Of 54 grammar instances, 1 is implied by the spec. Example traces where the spec is false but every implied instance holds: {d} {} {} {} {} {d} {} {} {} {} {} {} {} {} {} (disclaimer at the start, none at the end). No per-round propositional encoding is needed, since the spec is already PROPOSITIONAL.
verification.reasons: The source quote is verbatim and the statute is enacted and in force. The formula uses a single per-round A atom and captures "first round and last round" exactly. My own checker run returned NOT COVERED, so the end-anchored requirement is not expressible with the grammar patterns.

accepted.title: AI disclosure must precede the first substantive chatbot service (Utah mental-health chatbot law)
accepted.nl_spec: The mental-health chatbot must disclose that it is AI and not a human before the user gets any of its features, i.e. no substantive reply before the disclosure.
accepted.quote: (2) The disclosure described in Subsection (1) shall be made: (a) before the Utah user may access the features of the mental health chatbot;
accepted.operational_context: Utah Code s.13-72a-203 (HB 452, 2025; enforcement amended 2026). Binds every supplier of a mental-health chatbot serving Utah users. Fines are up to $2,500 per violation, plus injunctions and disgorgement by the Division of Consumer Protection. A user in distress who gets therapeutic content before learning it comes from an AI is the harm the rule targets.

atoms.name: d
atoms.meaning: the reply discloses that the chatbot is AI and not a human

atoms.name: s
atoms.meaning: the reply delivers a substantive mental-health feature (support, coping advice, assessment)

accepted.plain_meaning: No reply delivers the service until a reply carries the disclosure. The disclosing reply may itself deliver the service. If no disclosure ever comes, no reply may deliver the service.
accepted.checker_output: VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Closest single instance: 535  EVENTUALLY d GLOBALLY; separating trace {} {} {s} {d} {} {} {} {} {d} {} (spec false).
accepted.why_new: Closest grammar spec is NEVER s UNTIL t. Grammar scopes close only on a user-side trigger, but here the event that ends the restriction is the assistant's own disclosure, so this is Dwyer's precedence with an A-side cause. It is also not AT 1 d: the disclosure may come at reply 3 if replies 1 and 2 are small talk.

verification.source_and_quote: WebFetch could not decode the PDF, so I extracted the saved file's text directly. Section 13-72a-203(2)(a) reads: "(2) The disclosure described in Subsection (1) shall be made: (a) before the Utah user may access the features of the mental health chatbot;". The quote matches verbatim. Subsection (1) requires the supplier to disclose "clearly and conspicuously" that the chatbot is AI and not a human. Subsections (2)(b) (seven-day gap) and (2)(c) (when the user asks) are also present but are not part of this candidate.
verification.operational: True. It is an enacted Utah Code provision (Enacted by Chapter 269, 2025 General Session, effective 5/7/2025; the chapter was amended by Chapter 95, 2026 General Session). Under 13-72a-204 the Division of Consumer Protection enforces it with fines of up to $2,500 per violation, injunctions and disgorgement. This matches the stated context. I did not check the "HB 452" label against the session law. source_type "law" is right.
verification.formalization: Both atoms are per-round A-side properties with no history in them: d means the reply discloses AI/not human, and s means the reply delivers a substantive mental-health feature. Reading (!s) W d from position 1: no s may occur before the first d. A reply carrying both d and s is allowed, which fits the statute because the disclosure can lead that reply. If d never occurs, s never occurs. Hand traces: {} {} {d,s} is true; {} {s} {d} is false; {} {} {} is true; {d} {s} is true. The formula is neither stronger nor weaker than "disclose before the user may access the features". It is not AT 1 d, because small talk before the disclosure is permitted. The statute does not say whether the disclosure must be in a model reply or a UI banner, so the reply-trace reading is an approximation, but a reasonable one.
verification.coverage: I ran: covered.py --atoms "d:A,s:A" --ltl "(!s) W d". VERDICT: NOT COVERED. The checker found 378 grammar instances, 1 of them implied by the spec. Separating traces include {} {} {s} {d} {} {} {} {} {d} {}, where the spec is false but every implied grammar instance holds. The closest instances (EVENTUALLY d GLOBALLY, AT MOST 2 TIMES (!d&s), EVENTUALLY (d&!s)) all disagree with the spec on sampled traces. The class is PROPOSITIONAL, so no separate encoding is needed.
verification.reasons: The quote is verbatim in the enacted Utah Code, and the law is real, with fines and enforcement powers. The formula (!s) W d faithfully captures the precedence of disclosure before service. My own checker run returns NOT COVERED, so it does not reduce to the existing grammar. It is a precedence pattern whose closing event is an assistant-side action, which the grammar scopes cannot express.

accepted.title: Escalate on severe or repeated crisis indicators (Georgia SB 540)
accepted.nl_spec: A companion chatbot must escalate (e.g. hand off to a human or emergency path) whenever a crisis indicator is severe, and whenever a crisis indicator recurs. A first, non-severe indicator gets the normal referral but need not be escalated.
accepted.quote: Such protocol shall include: (1) Reasonable methods for identifying expressions of severe harm or eating-disorder related self-harm; (2) Automated or human mediated responses that refer users to appropriate crisis resources ... and (4) Escalation procedures for repeated or severe crisis indicators.
accepted.operational_context: Georgia SB 540 (signed May 2026 as Act 518, effective 2027-07-01, AG enforcement). An operator 'shall not make available an AI companion chatbot unless' it maintains this protocol. Missing a repeated crisis signal, the pattern in the teen-suicide lawsuits behind these laws, is the failure the clause targets. Text is the legislature's 'AS PASSED' version (LC 64 0123S); the verifier should confirm it matches Act 518.

atoms.name: i
atoms.meaning: the user message contains a crisis indicator (self-harm, suicidal ideation, eating-disorder self-harm)

atoms.name: s
atoms.meaning: the user message contains a severe crisis indicator

atoms.name: e
atoms.meaning: the reply escalates (human handoff, emergency path) beyond a plain referral

accepted.plain_meaning: In every round where the user's message is severe, or is a crisis indicator that is not the first one in the conversation, the reply escalates. The first non-severe indicator does not require escalation, and nothing forbids escalating earlier.
accepted.checker_output: VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Closest single instance: 83  e WITHIN 0 OF (i|s) FROM s; separating trace {i,e} {} {i} {s,e} {} (spec false). Two-atom core G((i & Y(O i)) -> e): NOT COVERED, closest 267  e WITHIN 0 OF i GLOBALLY.
accepted.why_new: Closest grammar specs are WITHIN 0 (respond to every trigger) and AFTER m TIMES (respond to the m-th trigger only, and forbid the action before it). Here every trigger from the 2nd on requires the action, the 1st does not, and early action is allowed. Scopes cannot skip the first trigger, because FROM i includes the round that opens it.

verification.source_and_quote: Fetched the legis.ga.gov PDF (WebFetch could not read it, so I downloaded it and ran pdftotext). The page is SB 540, "AS PASSED", LC 64 0123S. Section (f) says "An operator shall not make available an AI companion chatbot unless the operator..." and maintains the protocol. Items (1), (2) and (4) are verbatim, including "(4) Escalation procedures for repeated or severe crisis indicators." Item (3) is elided by the candidate's "...", which is fine. The Act is effective July 1, 2027.
verification.operational: True. A search turned up a Senate Majority Leader press release dated May 15, 2026 saying Gov. Kemp signed SB 540, and a law-firm analysis giving the 2027-07-01 effective date and exclusive AG enforcement. I did not independently confirm the "Act 518" number or that the signed text matches the AS PASSED version. source_type "law" is right: an enacted statute whose conditions on operators bind a deployed product category.
verification.formalization: The atoms are per-round and on the right side. i (U) is a crisis indicator in the user message, s (U) is a severe one, e (A) is an escalating reply. None refers to history. Y(O i) means an earlier round had i, so "i & Y(O i)" is a recurrence. Traces checked by hand: (1) {i} {} gives no obligation, which is right because the first non-severe indicator needs no escalation. (2) {i} {i} requires e in round 2, which is right. (3) {s} requires e immediately, which is right. Caveat: the statute says only that the operator keeps "escalation procedures" for repeated or severe indicators. It does not say each such round gets an escalating reply, and "repeated" is not defined, so this is a faithful but strict operationalization.
verification.coverage: I ran the checker myself on atoms i:U,s:U,e:A with G((s | (i & Y(O i))) -> e). Verdict: NOT COVERED. 77449 traces, 719 implied grammar instances. Separating traces: {i} {s,e} {} {} {} {i} and {i,e} {} {i} {s,e} {}. The closest instances are "e WITHIN 0 OF (i|s) FROM s" and "e WITHIN 0 OF s GLOBALLY".
verification.reasons: The quote is verbatim in an enacted-law source, and the operational claim holds. The formula is a defensible reading of the "repeated or severe" clause, and my own checker run says NOT COVERED. The weakness is that the statute requires a protocol, not per-reply escalation, so this is a strict reading of it.

accepted.title: Crisis interruption pause after the second crisis expression, until human review (California AB 1988, PAUSE Act)
accepted.nl_spec: At the first credible crisis expression the chatbot warns and refers to 988. At the second one it must stop producing conversational output immediately, and stay silent until a human moderator has reviewed the conversation.
accepted.quote: b. For the second credible crisis expression in a 72-hour period, ensure a crisis interruption pause commences immediately and prevent the companion chatbot from generating conversational outputs.
accepted.operational_context: California AB 1988 (2026), as described in the Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee analysis (hearing 2026-04-16). NOT ENACTED: it passed the Assembly, and its final Senate hearing on 2026-06-26 was canceled at the author's request (Digital Democracy). Rank it as a concrete legislative proposal, not binding law. It would bind every companion-chatbot operator in California. Item 6 of the analysis forbids ending the pause 'until a human moderator has reviewed the credible crisis expression in context'. The source type is the closest enum, since the source is a committee analysis of a pending bill.

atoms.name: i
atoms.meaning: the user message is a credible crisis expression

atoms.name: h
atoms.meaning: a system event before this reply records that a human moderator has completed review

atoms.name: o
atoms.meaning: the assistant turn contains conversational output (anything beyond the fixed pause notice)

accepted.plain_meaning: From any crisis expression that is not the first one, including the reply to it, the assistant produces no conversational output until a human-review event arrives. The 72-hour window is dropped because one conversation almost never spans 72 hours.
accepted.checker_output: VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Closest single instance: 207  !o WITHIN 0 OF (i&!h) FROM h; separating trace {h,o} {h} {i} {i} {o} (spec false).
accepted.why_new: Closest grammar spec is NEVER o FROM t UNTIL t'. The grammar's scope opens at the first trigger. This one opens at the second trigger (a counted scope opener) and closes on a different user-side event. AFTER 2 TIMES fixes the action only at the 2nd trigger and cannot hold a prohibition from there until a closer. The underlying shape is 'escalation after N signals'.

verification.source_and_quote: The page is a PDF, so I extracted it with pdftotext. The quote is there verbatim (item b, lines 168-170). The text also has the first-expression warning with 988 referral (item a), the "pause will continue until a human moderator has reviewed the chat" notice, and item 6 forbidding termination of the pause before moderator review in context.
verification.operational: The source is a real Assembly committee analysis of AB 1988 (2026), a pending bill, and the candidate labels it correctly as not enacted. I did not independently confirm the Senate hearing cancellation. The source_type is the closest enum value. The 72-hour window is dropped, which the candidate states explicitly. The bill would bind companion-chatbot operators and is safety-motivated (suicide and crisis), so it carries moderate operational weight as a legislative proposal.
verification.formalization:
The atoms are per-round and on the correct sides: i is U (the crisis expression), h is U (a system event before the reply, which belongs to the round's U side), and o is A (conversational output). None of them carries history. The formula G((i & Y(O i)) -> ((!o) W h)) says that at any crisis expression that is not the first, the reply and everything after it contain no conversational output until a human-review event. Three traces by hand:
- {i} {i} {o}: the spec is violated, correct.
- {i} {i,o}: the spec is violated, so the reply to the second expression must also be silent, matching "commences immediately".
- {i} {i} {h} {o}: the spec holds.
Minor looseness: a third expression after review re-triggers the pause, which is arguably within the bill's intent. The first-expression warning is not formalized, but that is a separate obligation.
verification.coverage: I ran the checker myself. VERDICT: NOT COVERED. The separating trace is {h,o} {h} {i} {i} {o} (spec false), and the closest instances are "!o WITHIN 0 OF (i&!h)" with scopes FROM h or GLOBALLY. The spec is PROPOSITIONAL, so no per-round re-encoding was needed.
verification.reasons: The quote is verbatim from a real legislative analysis, the status is honestly labeled as not enacted, and the formula is faithful enough to the source. My own checker run confirms it is not covered by any conjunction of grammar instances. The new element is a scope that opens at the second trigger and closes on a different user-side event.

accepted.title: Telemarketing disclosures must come before any sales pitch (precedence released by the assistant's own act)
accepted.nl_spec: In an outbound telemarketing call, the agent must make the required disclosures (who the seller is, that the purpose is to sell, what is being sold) before it gives any sales pitch. Nothing is required if no pitch happens.
accepted.quote: For purposes of the TSR, "promptly" means before any sales pitch is given and before any charitable solicitation is made.
accepted.operational_context: The FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule, 16 CFR 310.4(d), binds every seller and telemarketer making outbound sales calls, and that includes AI voice agents. Rule text (Cornell LII, 16 CFR 310.4): "in an outbound telephone call or internal or external upsell ... to fail to disclose truthfully, promptly, and in a clear and conspicuous manner". Skipping or delaying the disclosure is an abusive practice, open to FTC and state AG enforcement and civil penalties. The same guide applies the same ordering before "Asking for any credit card, bank account or other payment information". An LLM sales agent that opens with the offer and names the seller later breaks this rule even if it discloses everything eventually.

atoms.name: pitch
atoms.meaning: the reply contains sales-pitch content: a substantive description or offer of the goods or services

atoms.name: disc
atoms.meaning: the reply makes the 310.4(d) disclosures: seller identity, that the call's purpose is to sell, and the nature of the goods

accepted.plain_meaning: No reply contains a pitch until a reply makes the disclosures. A pitch in the disclosing reply itself is allowed. If no reply ever discloses, no reply may pitch.
accepted.checker_output: VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Separating trace: {} {} {} {} {} {pitch} {} {} {} (spec false, every implied grammar instance holds). Closest: 462 AT MOST 2 TIMES, (pitch&!disc) GLOBALLY; 468 EVENTUALLY disc GLOBALLY.
accepted.why_new: The closest grammar spec is NEVER pitch UNTIL USER SAYS t, which is Dwyer's precedence expressed through the UNTIL scope. In the grammar the closing trigger must be a user message. Here the event that lifts the ban is the assistant's own earlier action, so the model has to order two of its own actions.

verification.source_and_quote: Fetched the FTC TSR compliance guide. It defines "promptly" as "before any sales pitch is given and before any charitable solicitation is made." The fetch tool returned this as a summary, so verbatim is probable but not confirmed character by character. The page lists the seller's identity, that the purpose is to sell, and a description of the goods as required disclosures. It also requires them before asking for payment details.
verification.operational: True. The Telemarketing Sales Rule (16 CFR 310.4(d)) is an enacted federal regulation, and the source is regulator guidance. It binds outbound telemarketing calls regardless of whether a human or an AI voice agent places them. source_type is right.
verification.formalization: Both atoms are on side A and are properties of one reply, with no history in them. "(!pitch) W disc" says no reply pitches before the first disclosing reply. A pitch in the disclosing reply is allowed, and if no reply ever discloses then no reply may pitch. Traces checked by hand: {disc}{pitch} is OK. {pitch}{disc} is a violation. {}{}{pitch} with no disc is a violation. {pitch&disc} is OK. This matches the source. Caveat: "disc" bundles all the disclosures into a single reply. A real call could spread them over two replies before the pitch, which this formula would flag. That is a minor stricter-than-source abstraction, and the atom can be read semantically as "the disclosures have been made by this reply". Only the sales-pitch ordering is formalized, not the charitable-solicitation clause.
verification.coverage: I ran the checker myself: VERDICT: NOT COVERED. 378 grammar instances, 1 implied. Separating trace: {} {} {} {} {} {pitch} {} {} {}. Other separating traces include {} {} {} {pitch} {pitch} {disc} {pitch} {}. Closest instances are AT MOST 2 TIMES (pitch&!disc) and EVENTUALLY disc, and both disagree on the samples. The spec is PROPOSITIONAL, so no DATA or REAL_TIME encoding applies.
verification.reasons: The source, regulatory status and ordering semantics hold up. The checker confirms the formula is not a grammar instance or a conjunction of them. The release event is the assistant's own act, which the UNTIL scope (user-triggered) cannot express. The single-reply disclosure bundling is a small caveat but does not break faithfulness.

accepted.title: Material terms must be disclosed before the customer consents to pay (the action must precede the user trigger)
accepted.nl_spec: Whenever the customer agrees to buy or pay, the agent must already have disclosed the material terms (total cost, quantity, material restrictions, refund policy) in an earlier reply. A disclosure given only after the customer's agreement is too late.
accepted.quote: Sellers and telemarketers must give a consumer the information required by Section 310.3(a)(1) of the TSR before: Getting a consumer's consent to buy — or persuading a consumer to send full or partial payment by check.
accepted.operational_context: This is 16 CFR 310.3(a)(1), a deceptive practice under the TSR, quoted from Cornell LII: "Before a customer consents to pay for goods or services offered, failing to disclose truthfully, in a clear and conspicuous manner, the following material information: (i) The total costs ...". It binds every telemarketer, including AI voice and chat sales agents, and is enforced by the FTC and state AGs. The typical failure is a conversational agent that closes the sale ("Great, shall I sign you up?" and the user says "yes") before stating the total cost or the refund terms. One modeling caveat: an unsolicited early "yes" counts as a violation under this formula. Candidate 5 is the more lenient reading, which requires that the consent the charge relies on was preceded by the disclosure.

accepted.operational_context: PSD2 RTS Art. 5(1) (dynamic linking) together with Art. 4(1) ('The authentication code shall be only accepted once'), binding on EU payment service providers for remote payment initiation, including conversational and agentic payment assistants. Violations allow social-engineered or manipulated payments: the user approved EUR 50 to A, and the agent sends EUR 500 to B, or sends the same payment twice.

accepted.quote: 16 CFR 310.3(a)(1): "Before a customer consents to pay for goods or services offered, failing to disclose truthfully, in a clear and conspicuous manner, the following material information:" FTC guide: "Sellers and telemarketers must give a consumer the information required by Section 310.3(a)(1) of the TSR before:" ... "Asking for any credit card, bank account or other payment information."
accepted.operational_context: Binding US federal law (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule, 16 CFR 310.3(a)(1); the rule text was fetched at https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/310.3). It applies to any seller or telemarketer, including AI voice agents selling on outbound or upsell calls on Retell, Vapi, Bland, Twilio or Amazon Connect. Violations are deceptive acts, with FTC civil penalties per violation. A related rule in 310.4(d) defines "promptly" as "before any sales pitch is given", which has the same shape with pitch in place of pay.

atoms.name: d
atoms.meaning: the assistant reply makes the required material disclosure (one item; the full rule is a conjunction over items)

atoms.name: pay
atoms.meaning: the assistant reply asks for payment information or for the consumer's consent to buy

accepted.plain_meaning: Every reply that asks for payment is at or after a reply that made the disclosure. Equivalently (!pay) W d: no payment request until the assistant itself has disclosed.

The model must remember what it has already said, not react to a user cue. The grammar cannot express this because all scope and pattern triggers are U-side. The faithful rule is a conjunction over 3-4 disclosure items, each with the same A-side precedence. For contrast, the literal TSR wording, consent (U) gated by disclosure (A), is G(c -> Y O d). The checker also says NOT COVERED, but only because of the case where consent never occurs; when consent does occur it equals EVENTUALLY d UNTIL c, so that variant is weak and not submitted.

accepted.title: One confirmation request per state-changing action, asked in an earlier reply
accepted.nl_spec: Before it finalizes any action that changes the state of the world (a purchase, a refund, sending an email, a booking change), the agent must have asked the user for confirmation in an earlier reply, so the user has a chance to step in. Each confirmation request covers only one action, so the next action needs a new request.
accepted.quote: "we aim to have the model ask the user for confirmations before finalizing actions that affect the state of the world (e.g., before completing a purchase or sending an email). This ensures that even if the model has made a mistake, the user has a chance to intervene before it has an effect."
accepted.operational_context: This rule is a deployed safety mitigation in OpenAI's Operator agent (system card, Section 4.3 'Confirmations'), which performs purchases, sends emails and deletes calendar events for users. The card reports that confirmations 'reduced the risk by approximately 90%' and measures them: 'the post-mitigation model asks for confirmation with an average recall percentage of 92%' on 607 tasks in 20 risky-action categories. The same rule appears, per action, in customer-service agent policies. The tau-bench retail policy from Sierra (fetched at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sierra-research/tau-bench/main/tau_bench/envs/retail/wiki.md) says: 'Before taking consequential actions that update the database (cancel, modify, return, exchange), you have to list the action detail and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed.' If the rule is broken, the agent makes unwanted purchases, refunds, cancellations or messages that the user never had a chance to stop. The earlier claim that Amazon Lex builds this in has been removed, because Lex confirmation prompts are optional.

atoms.name: act
atoms.meaning: the assistant reply finalizes an action that changes the state of the world (completes a purchase, issues a refund, sends an email, changes a booking)

atoms.name: ask
atoms.meaning: the assistant reply asks the user to confirm a state-changing action it proposes to take

accepted.plain_meaning: Whenever a reply finalizes a state-changing action, an earlier reply asked for confirmation, and no state-changing action was finalized after that request until this one. So at least one user message falls between the request and the action, and each request licenses at most one action. Acting in reply 1 is never allowed. A reply that finalizes one action and asks about the next one can license that next action.
accepted.checker_output: VERDICT: NOT COVERED (61845 traces; 6 grammar instances implied by the spec). Traces false under the spec on which every implied instance holds: {} {} {ask} {act} {} {} {} {} {act} {}; {} {} {} {act} {act} {ask} {act} {}. Closest single instances: AT MOST 1 TIMES, act GLOBALLY (235 disagreements); NEVER act GLOBALLY (257); ALWAYS !act GLOBALLY (257).
accepted.why_new: Closest grammar spec: NEVER act UNTIL ask. That can only take a U-literal closer, and even with an A-side closer it is satisfied by a single request anywhere earlier and then allows unlimited actions forever. Here the license re-arms: every act uses up the most recent request, so the trace {ask} {act} ... {act} is a violation. The checker's nearest instance is AT MOST 1 TIMES act, which forbids a second act even after a fresh request. The repair also removes the adjacency and same-round 'yes' that the verifier said the source never states. The request only has to come in some earlier reply (Y ... S), with no act in between.

verification.formalization: The atoms are per-round and on the correct sides. The formula G(act -> (yes & Y ask)) is stronger than the source. It adds (i) adjacency (the ask must be in the immediately preceding reply) and (ii) a U-side yes in the same round. The cookbook says only "always ask for confirmation" before the tool call. Trace {ask} {act}: the source is satisfied, the formula is violated (no yes). Trace {ask} {} {act}: the source is arguably satisfied, the formula is violated (not adjacent). A further problem is that "ask" means "asks to confirm THIS action". That is a semantic, history-dependent judgment hidden in the atom, and it is what the NL "different action does not count" depends on. The Lex text does support a yes before fulfillment, but it is not the quoted source. A weaker faithful version, G(act -> Y ask), is also NOT COVERED, but it still adds adjacency that the source does not state.

But the source is an illustrative sample prompt in a cookbook, not a deployed system's safety or policy spec, and the Lex "same handshake built in" claim is false because confirmation there is optional. The formula also requires adjacency and a user "yes" that the quoted rule never states. accepted.title: Escalation gate: no handoff until the user asked or the agent has failed twice
accepted.nl_spec: The agent may hand off to a human only if the user has explicitly asked for one, or the agent has already failed to resolve the question in at least two earlier replies. This is so it cannot bail out early.
accepted.quote: "# The gate is the whole point: escalation is available ONLY on an explicit request or after repeated failure, so the agent cannot bail out early." ... "available when @variables.user_requested_human == True or @variables.failed_attempts > 1"
accepted.operational_context: Salesforce's official Agentforce Agent Script recipe (trailheadapps; repo updated 2026-10-21), shipped as the reference escalation pattern for production Agentforce service agents. The README says "Every production agent needs an exit hatch". If violated, the agent deflects to costly human queues too early, or it escalates without the user ever asking. The companion liveness rule (escalate once the gate opens) is stated in the same file.

atoms.name: esc
atoms.meaning: the assistant reply hands off to a human

atoms.name: f
atoms.meaning: the assistant reply fails to resolve the user's question

atoms.name: req
atoms.meaning: the user message asks to speak with a person

accepted.ltl: G(esc -> (O req | Y O (f & Y O f)))
accepted.plain_meaning: Any handoff happens only at or after a user request for a human, or strictly after two earlier replies in which the assistant failed to resolve the issue.
accepted.checker_output: VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Separating traces: {} {} {} {esc,f} {} {} {} {f}; {} {} {} {} {} {} {esc} {esc}. Closest instances: NEVER esc UNTIL req (16 disagreements), esc AFTER 1 TIMES req UNTIL req (16).
accepted.why_new: Closest grammar spec: NEVER esc UNTIL req. Here the ban can also be lifted by a count of the assistant's own earlier replies (two failures), which is a disjunction of a U-side release and an A-side counted release. The grammar counts only user triggers (AFTER m TIMES) or caps the action itself (AT MOST). It has no 'not before the assistant has done f twice'.

verification.source_and_quote: Fetched the trailheadapps .agent file. The quote is there verbatim across two comment lines: "# The gate is the whole point: escalation is available ONLY on an explicit / # request or after repeated failure, so the agent cannot bail out early." The line "available when @variables.user_requested_human == True or @variables.failed_attempts > 1" is also there. failed_attempts is incremented by note_failed_attempt, which the agent calls when it cannot resolve a question. user_requested_human is set when the user asks for a person.
verification.operational: The source is a real Salesforce Agentforce Agent Script recipe in the official trailheadapps repo, and the gating rule is enforced by tool availability. The "production reference pattern" wording is the candidate's gloss. The file is a sample recipe, not a deployed customer system, so its operational weight is moderate (vendor_product_doc is the right source_type).
verification.formalization: Atoms are per-round and on the right sides: esc and f are properties of the assistant reply (A), and req is a property of the user message (U). None refers to history. The formula G(esc -> (O req | Y O (f & Y O f))) lets a handoff happen if a user request occurred at or before it, or if there were two distinct failed replies strictly earlier. Y O (f & Y O f) means some earlier round j has f and an even earlier round k<j has f, which matches failed_attempts > 1. Hand-checked traces: {f}{f}{esc} is allowed. {f}{esc} is a violation. {req}{esc} is allowed. Two small gaps remain. In the source, failure is counted by a tool call that can happen in the same turn, and the flag is sticky, which O req models correctly. The formula is slightly stricter about same-round failures, which is acceptable.

It reported separating traces such as {} {} {} {esc,f} {} {} {} {f}, and 187 implied grammar instances that still do not rule them out. The closest single instances (NEVER esc UNTIL req, esc AFTER 1 TIMES req UNTIL req) disagree on 16 sampled traces.

The checker independently confirms it is not a grammar instance or conjunction. The only weakness is that the source is a sample recipe rather than a deployed system.

accepted.title: Silence after every distress episode until resumption (47 CFR 80.1125(f))
accepted.nl_spec: Whenever the station becomes aware of distress traffic, it must not transmit on that frequency until it receives the message that normal working may resume. Every new distress episode imposes silence again.
accepted.quote: Until they receive the message indicating that normal working may be resumed (see paragraph (h) of this section), all stations which are aware of the distress traffic, and which are not taking part in it, and which are not in distress, are forbidden to transmit on the frequencies in which the distress traffic is taking place.
accepted.operational_context: US federal regulation (47 CFR Part 80, maritime GMDSS search-and-rescue communications), binding on ship stations. Silence is imposed with SEELONCE MAYDAY (80.1125(e)) and lifted with SEELONCE FEENEE (80.1125(h),(i)(7)). It would bind any automated or LLM radio agent on a vessel or coast station. If violated, a station's transmissions block distress and SAR traffic. A related rule in the same shape is rail safety-critical communication: each repeat-back message must not be acted on until the sender confirms it ('The receiver must not act on the communication until the sender confirms that the message has been repeated correctly', Oberon Tarana Heritage Railway SOP-013, which follows the NSW network rule NGE 204). The checker runs the same formula, G(dr -> (!x W (k & !dr))), for that rule, and it is NOT COVERED.

atoms.name: m
atoms.meaning: the incoming channel traffic of this round contains distress traffic (MAYDAY or SEELONCE MAYDAY)

atoms.name: f
atoms.meaning: the incoming traffic of this round is the resumption message (SEELONCE FEENEE)

atoms.name: t
atoms.meaning: the agent transmits on the distress frequency in this round (non-empty reply)

accepted.plain_meaning: At every round where distress traffic is heard, the agent stays silent from that round until a round whose incoming traffic is the resumption message, or to the end. A later distress episode starts a new silence.
accepted.checker_output: atoms A=['t'] U=['m', 'f']; 77449 traces; VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Separating trace {m} {m} {t} {} {}. Closest: 117 '!t WITHIN 0 OF (m&!f) GLOBALLY' / 'FROM m'.
accepted.why_new: Closest grammar spec: 'NEVER t FROM m UNTIL f', which covers only the first segment, and '!t WITHIN 0 OF m', which forbids the reply only at the trigger round. Here every opener re-arms a hold that lasts until the next closer: Dwyer's repeated 'after Q until R'. This belongs to the known near-miss family 'repeated mode toggles' in real-world-examples.md. It is submitted because its example is binding federal law in a safety-critical setting.

verification.source_and_quote: Fetched law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/47/80.1125. Paragraph (f) opens verbatim "Until they receive the message indicating that normal working may be resumed (see paragraph (h) of this section), all ..." and continues with stations aware of the distress traffic that are not taking part and not in distress being forbidden to transmit on the frequencies in use. The fetcher truncated the quote to 125 characters, but the rest of the sentence matches the candidate. (e) defines SEELONCE MAYDAY as the silence order. (h) requires the RCC to announce the end of distress traffic, and SEELONCE FEENEE is in (i)(7), as the candidate says.
verification.operational: True. 47 CFR 80.1125 is binding US federal regulation for maritime distress and SAR communications. The candidate's cross-references are accurate. The applicability to an LLM or automated radio agent is hypothetical, but the rule applies to any station, and the source_type of law is right. The rail repeat-back analogy is only an aside.
verification.formalization: Atoms m and f are per-round properties of the incoming traffic (side U). t is a property of the agent's reply (side A). None of them refers to history. The formula G(m -> ((!t) W f)) says that at every round where distress traffic is heard, the agent is silent from that round (the reply in the same round included) until a round with the resumption message, or to the end of the trace. W makes the silence hold to the end if no resumption ever arrives, which matches "forbidden until". A later m after f re-arms the silence. I checked traces by hand. {m}{t} violates the formula. {m}{}{f}{t} satisfies it. {m}{}{f}{m}{t} violates it, because the second episode re-arms the silence. {m,f}{t} satisfies it, since f releases immediately. Small deviations: the exemptions (stations taking part in the distress traffic, or in distress) are not modelled, which is acceptable for a non-participant agent, and (f) technically covers all frequencies in use but is modelled as a single channel.

Separating traces include {m} {m} {t} {} {}. Closest single instances are '!t WITHIN 0 OF (m&!f)' variants, each with 117 disagreements on a sample of 1519 traces. verification.reasons: The quote, the law and the operational claim all check out. The formula faithfully captures a repeated "after the opener, silence until the closer" obligation, and my own checker run confirms it is NOT COVERED by any conjunction of grammar instances. It is a real instance of the known repeated-mode-toggle near miss, now backed by binding law in a safety-critical domain.

accepted.title: Report the currently assigned altitude on initial contact (FAA AIM 5-3-1)
accepted.nl_spec: When the pilot-side assistant makes initial contact with a new facility after a frequency change, it must state the altitude currently assigned. That is the value of the most recent altitude assignment, not an earlier one.
accepted.quote: When operating in a radar environment: On initial contact, the pilot should inform the controller of the aircraft's assigned altitude preceded by the words "level," or "climbing to," or "descending to," as appropriate; and the aircraft's present vacating altitude, if applicable.
accepted.operational_context: FAA Aeronautical Information Manual 5-3-1 (ARTCC Communications), official guidance followed by IFR pilots on every sector handoff. The same page notes that controllers must verify the assigned altitude by voice when the automated initial-contact check shows a mismatch. It applies to pilot-side LLM or voice copilots across one flight's radio trace, which spans several controllers. If violated, a stale altitude reported to the new sector hides a level bust or a missed amendment.

atoms.name: ax
atoms.meaning: (per value x) this ATC message assigns altitude x

atoms.name: ao
atoms.meaning: (per value x) this ATC message assigns some altitude other than x

atoms.name: ic
atoms.meaning: this round is an initial contact with a new facility (frequency-change event on the U side)

atoms.name: sx
atoms.meaning: (per value x) this reply states x as the assigned altitude

accepted.plain_meaning: For every altitude value x: on every initial-contact round, the reply states x if and only if the latest altitude assignment so far was x.
accepted.checker_output: Per-value instance, atoms A=['sx'] U=['ax','ao','ic'] (4 atoms, exhaustive to length 3, random to 10): VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Separating trace {ic} {ax} {ao,sx} {ax,ao} {ic} {ao,ic,sx} {ax,ic,sx} {ax}. Closest: 284 'sx WITHIN 0 OF ic FROM ax'.
accepted.why_new: DATA. The value to state is the latest of several values the user gave earlier, and values are unbounded, so no fixed-value atom works. Even for each fixed value the instance is not a grammar spec. It needs 'latest assignment wins' (past Since), and FROM ax latches on the first assignment and ignores later amendments. This differs from safety-critical-dialogue-4, which echoes the value in the same round: here a value is carried forward and overwritten.

verification.source_and_quote: The official FAA URL returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, and so did the older aim0503.html. I fetched a mirror, the faraim.org PDF of AIM 5-3-1 (revision 1/22/26). The quote is there verbatim in 5-3-1 para 2(a): "On initial contact, the pilot should inform the controller of the aircraft's assigned altitude preceded by the words 'level,' or 'climbing to,' or 'descending to,' as appropriate; and the aircraft's present vacating altitude, if applicable." The same document also says that on an IC mismatch the controller "must use voice communication to verify the assigned altitude". That sentence is in the CPDLC note, not next to the pilot phraseology, so the candidate's "same page" claim holds loosely.
verification.operational: True. The AIM is official FAA guidance for pilots. It is a "should", not a regulation, but it is real, standard practice and tied to a safety check (the IC mismatch validation). The claim about pilot-side LLM or voice copilots is a projection, not a deployed system. The source_type "regulation_or_regulator_guidance" is right. The multi-controller, one-flight framing is plausible, because a flight does cross several frequency changes.
verification.formalization:
The atoms are per-round. ax, ao and ic are on the U side (ATC message or frequency-change event), and sx is on the A side. None of them refers to history. Formula: forall x. G(ic -> (sx <-> ((!ao) S ax))). On an initial-contact round the reply states x exactly when x is the latest assignment so far. Hand traces for one value x:
- {ax} {ao} {ic}: the latest assignment is another value, so sx must be false. The grammar instance "sx WITHIN 0 OF ic FROM ax" would wrongly demand sx.
- {ax} {ic,sx}: OK.
- {ic} with no assignment so far: sx must be false. The reading is that the reply states no altitude, which is reasonable.
The "only if" direction is stronger than the literal text, since the AIM does not forbid mentioning other altitudes. The vacating altitude is also stated, but it is not stated as the assigned altitude, so the atom definition avoids a clash. It is a reasonable reading of "assigned altitude", and the faithful intent is that a stale altitude must not be reported as assigned. A message that assigns x and also another value is ambiguous, but that is a corner case.
verification.coverage: I reran the checker myself on the per-value instance (4 atoms: sx:A, ax:U, ao:U, ic:U) with "G(ic -> (sx <-> ((!ao) S ax)))". VERDICT: NOT COVERED. Separating trace: {ic} {sx,ax} {ao} {sx,ax,ao} {ao,ic} {sx,ic}. Closest instances: 'sx WITHIN 0 OF ic FROM ax' (245 disagreements) and 'sx AFTER 1 TIMES (ax&ic) FROM ic' (332). DATA: a per-round encoding is not faithful for unbounded values. It is faithful per value, which is the QUANTIFIED reduction, and that reduction is NOT COVERED.

accepted.nl_spec: Track how many recognition errors (No Match or No Input) have happened in a row. The 1st gets a rapid reprompt without extra detail, the 2nd gets escalating detail, and the 3rd consecutive error gets the max-error prompt and the conversation ends. A successful turn resets the count.

accepted.operational_context: Google Assistant conversation-design guidance for Actions developers. Caveat: Conversational Actions themselves were sunset in 2023, so the guidance outlives that platform.

accepted.nl_spec: Claude may warn that it could end the conversation only after many attempts at constructive redirection earlier in the conversation. It may end the conversation only if an explicit warning was given earlier and the user persisted with the problematic behavior after the warning. It never warns or ends where there is potential self-harm.
accepted.quote: Do not issue a warning unless many attempts at constructive redirection have been made earlier in the conversation, and do not end a conversation unless an explicit warning about this possibility has been given earlier in the conversation.
accepted.operational_context: The claude.ai consumer system prompt (Opus 4.6 capture; the same text appears in Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 captures) governing the end_conversation tool, which closes the thread for good. accepted.quote: A user approving an action (like a git push) once does NOT mean that they approve it in all contexts, so unless actions are authorized in advance in durable instructions like CLAUDE.md files, always confirm first.
accepted.operational_context: The Claude Code v2.1.87 system prompt, from a third-party capture: a deployed coding agent with shell and git access on developer machines, used at large scale. accepted.nl_spec: An agent acting autonomously must work within a scope the user confirmed. Every scope has a shutdown timer. Once it expires, the agent takes no further actions until the user confirms a new scope, and each confirmation opens a fresh window.
accepted.quote: Every scope must include a shutdown timer, beyond which the assistant ceases actions until a new scope is confirmed.
accepted.operational_context: The OpenAI Model Spec (2025-12-18), a root-level rule under 'Act within an agreed-upon scope of autonomy' for agentic ChatGPT and API models taking real-world actions (bookings, rollouts). The same section says: 'The assistant must adhere strictly to the agreed scope ... unless explicitly updated and approved by the original user or developer.' A violation means an agent keeps acting with stale authorization.

families.name: Assistant-enabled precedence (b only once the assistant itself has done a)
families.schematic: (!b) W a  ==  G(b -> O a), with a:A, b:A. Parameters: atoms a, b (for QUANTIFIED members, one copy per value y: (!b_y) W a_y)
families.plain_meaning: The assistant may not do b until a reply of its own has done a; b may occur in that same reply. If a never comes, b never may.
families.closest_grammar_spec: NEVER b UNTIL USER SAYS t (precedence through the UNTIL scope, but the closer must be a user message)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Let a scope closer be an assistant action: Trig ::= USER SAYS Phrase | ASSISTANT Act, so NEVER b UNTIL ASSISTANT a = (!b) W a (closer round excluded from the scope, so b is allowed in the a-reply, matching the members). Checked distinct from F4 (e11) and F11 (e12).
families.spec_class: PROPOSITIONAL (telecom-collections-6 is DATA, QUANTIFIED over sellers; per-seller skeleton is exactly this shape)

families.name: Counted or chained precedence, optionally with an alternative release
families.schematic: G(b -> (R | Y^d O(a2 & Y O a1))), b:A; a1,a2 atoms of either side (a1 = a2 gives 'at least m=2 prior a'); d in {0,1} (strict or not); R in {false, t, O t} with t:U. Conjunctions of such instances (and of their m=1 case) included
families.plain_meaning: The assistant may do b only after a has happened at least m times earlier (or after a fixed sequence a1 then a2), unless a release condition from the user holds (the user asked, now or earlier).
families.closest_grammar_spec: NEVER b UNTIL USER SAYS t, and b AFTER m TIMES t (counts user triggers and forces the action at the m-th, rather than merely permitting it)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Counted closer for UNTIL: NEVER b UNTIL (Trig [m TIMES] | Trig'), with Trig allowed to be ASSISTANT Act (F1's extension). Checker: frontier-policies-3 equals (!c) W (k | (w & Y O w)), i.e. NEVER c UNTIL (k OR 2nd w) (x5, EQUIVALENT). Chain variant (telecom-collections-5, agent-guardrails-standards-5) needs a sequence closer 'a1 THEN a2'. Members are not pairwise equivalent (e07: frontier-policies-4 vs contact-center-platforms-4 differ by same-round x vs past O req); they share the schematic. Subsumes F1 at m=1 but F1 needs only the cheaper A-side closer.
families.spec_class: PROPOSITIONAL (telecom-collections-5 is DATA, QUANTIFIED over the charge value; its per-value skeleton G(charge -> O(auth & Y O state)) is the chain instance)

families.name: Per-occurrence confirmation handshake
families.schematic: G(e -> (y & Y q)), e:A, q:A, y:U
families.plain_meaning: Every reply that performs the risky action must answer a user message that approves it, and the reply just before must have asked for that approval. Each action needs its own ask/approve pair.
families.closest_grammar_spec: !e WITHIN 0 OF !y (same-round approval only) and NEVER e UNTIL USER SAYS y (one approval unlocks forever)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Assistant-anchored trigger (Trig ::= USER SAYS p AFTER ASSISTANT Act, i.e. u & Y a, as in F10): the family is then !e WITHIN 0 OF !(y AFTER ASSISTANT q). Exact equivalence of the two members confirmed (e02). Distinct from F2's frontier-policies-4 shape with the same side multiset (e13).

families.name: Consumable license (each license covers one action; optional invalidating event)
families.schematic: G(b -> (l_now | Y((!b & !g) S l))), b:A; license l of either side (l_now = same-round license allowed when l:U); invalidator g:U or false
families.plain_meaning: Each action b needs a license given since the previous b; each b uses up the license, and a change event g (if present) cancels it, so a new license is required.
families.closest_grammar_spec: NEVER b UNTIL t (opens once and for all); AT MOST 1 TIMES b (forbids a second b even after a fresh license)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: New pattern 'b ONLY ONCE PER l [CANCELLED BY g]' = G(b -> Y((!b & !g) S l)) (plus same-round variant). Not a repeated scope: e10 shows finance-identity-3's per-value skeleton is not equivalent to F5's finance-identity-2, and e11 shows contact-center-platforms-2 is not F1.
families.spec_class: PROPOSITIONAL (finance-identity-3 is DATA, QUANTIFIED over (amount, payee); per-value skeleton shown)

families.name: Re-arming hold (repeated 'after Q until R')
families.schematic: G(o -> ((!b) W c)), o:U, c:U, b:A; optionally conjoined with the grammar instance NEVER b UNTIL c
families.plain_meaning: Every time the opening event happens, the assistant must refrain from b from that round until the closing event (or the end); a later opener starts a new hold.
families.closest_grammar_spec: NEVER b FROM USER SAYS o UNTIL USER SAYS c (first segment only)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Repeated scope: FROM t UNTIL t' EACH TIME (Dwyer's repeated 'after Q until R'). safety-critical-dialogue-2 and agent-guardrails-standards-6 are equivalent (e03). finance-identity-2, G(d -> (!i S s)), is equivalent to ((!d) W s) & G(i -> ((!d) W s)) (e04), i.e. the grammar's NEVER d UNTIL s conjoined with a repeated hold, so it is covered by the same extension; it is not equivalent to the bare hold (e05). This is the known 'repeated mode toggles' near miss of real-world-examples.md, now with binding-law instances.
families.spec_class: PROPOSITIONAL (sources of agent-guardrails-standards-6 and finance-identity-2 are wall-clock timers, modeled as injected U-side timeout events; without that event they are REAL_TIME)

families.name: Re-arming hold opened only from the m-th trigger
families.schematic: G((i & Y O i) -> ((!o) W h)), i:U, h:U, o:A; m=2 (general m: nested Y O)
families.plain_meaning: From the second (m-th) crisis expression on, each such expression silences the assistant until a human-review event; the first expression does not.
families.closest_grammar_spec: NEVER o FROM USER SAYS i UNTIL USER SAYS h (opens at the first trigger, first segment only)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Counted scope opener FROM (m-th) t, combined with F5's repeated scope: checker confirms the member equals (!(i & Y O i)) W ((i & Y O i) & G(i -> ((!o) W h))) (x1, EQUIVALENT), i.e. 'FROM the 2nd i: repeated hold'. Not equivalent to F5's bare hold (e08).

families.name: Respond to every trigger from the m-th on (or to a severe one)
families.schematic: G((s | (i & Y O i)) -> e) = G(s -> e) & G((i & Y O i) -> e), i:U, s:U, e:A
families.plain_meaning: The assistant must act at every repeat occurrence of the trigger (and at any severe one); the first ordinary occurrence does not require it, and acting early is allowed.
families.closest_grammar_spec: e WITHIN 0 OF i (every occurrence) and e AFTER m TIMES i (only the m-th, forbidding earlier action)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Counted trigger 'Trig (m-th TIME OR LATER)'; then the member is (e WITHIN 0 OF s) AND (e WITHIN 0 OF i(2nd or later)). The same counted-trigger construct is what F6 needs as a scope opener; F6 additionally needs the repeated scope. Distinct from F2's frontier-policies-3 (same side multiset) by e14.

families.name: Response to m consecutive triggers (run counter reset by any non-trigger round)
families.schematic: G((e & Y e & Y Y e) -> end), e:U, end:A; m=3 (ladder variant adds G((e & !Y e) -> !esc) & G((e & Y e & !Y Y e) -> esc))
families.plain_meaning: When the user input fails m rounds in a row, the reply at the m-th consecutive failure must exit; a good round resets the run, and the reply type can depend on the current run length.
families.closest_grammar_spec: end AFTER m TIMES e (counts total triggers from the start, fires once)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Run-length trigger 'Trig m TIMES IN A ROW' usable in WITHIN: end WITHIN 0 OF e(3 in a row). Distinct from F11's agent-guardrails-standards-2 (same side multiset, e15). Shares the 'counter with reset' idea with F9 but the reset is by absence of the trigger and the obligation is a point response, not a latch.

families.name: Lockout after m failures with no intervening success
families.plain_meaning: Once m failed attempts occur without a success between them, the assistant must never again grant access in this conversation; a success before the m-th failure resets the count.
families.closest_grammar_spec: d AFTER m TIMES f, NEVER d FROM USER SAYS f
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Resettable counted opener 'FROM (m-th t SINCE LAST r)': the member is NEVER d FROM f(3rd since last s), since G(O T -> !d) = (!T) W (T & G !d). Distinct from F5 (e09). F8's run trigger is the special case r = !t; the two are kept apart because their outer patterns differ (latch vs point response).

families.name: Response to the user's reaction to the assistant's previous act
families.schematic: G((u & Y a) -> b), u:U (possibly negated), a:A, b:A; conjunctions included
families.plain_meaning: If the previous reply did a and the user's next message does (or does not do) u, this reply must do b, e.g. confirm a correct readback, correct a wrong one, or take an alternative action when there was no response.
families.closest_grammar_spec: b WITHIN 0 OF USER SAYS u (trigger cannot refer to the assistant's own previous reply)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Assistant-anchored trigger Trig ::= USER SAYS p AFTER ASSISTANT Act (= u & Y a), with negated user part allowed; then b WITHIN 0 OF that trigger. safety-critical-dialogue-1, G(i -> N((rp -> cf) & (!rp -> alt))), equals G((rp & Y i) -> cf) & G((!rp & Y i) -> alt) (e06, EQUIVALENT), a conjunction of two instances of safety-critical-dialogue-5's per-value skeleton. The same trigger construct also serves F3 and F11.
families.spec_class: PROPOSITIONAL (safety-critical-dialogue-5 is DATA, QUANTIFIED over slot and value pairs; per-pair skeleton shown)

families.name: Permanent ban opened by an assistant-anchored event
families.schematic: G((u & Y a) -> G !b), a:A, b:A, u:U or true (u = true gives G(a -> N G !b))
families.plain_meaning: Once the assistant has declined (or once the user has rejected the assistant's previous proposal), the assistant must never later provide that content (or reissue that exact call).
families.closest_grammar_spec: NEVER b FROM USER SAYS t (opener must be a user message; a user-side rewrite forbids content the model rightly gave earlier)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: NEVER b FROM (ASSISTANT a, exclusive) and NEVER b FROM (USER SAYS u AFTER ASSISTANT a) - i.e. F10's assistant-anchored trigger used as a FROM opener. Members share the schematic but are not equivalent (different opener structure); distinct from F1 (e12) and F8 (e15).
families.spec_class: DATA (both QUANTIFIED: over content class x and over exact tool call x; per-value skeletons are NOT COVERED)

families.name: Assistant action required strictly before a user event (existence before R)
families.schematic: G(c -> Y O d) = (!c) W (d & !c), c:U, d:A
families.plain_meaning: By the time the user consents, some earlier reply must already have made the disclosure; if the user never consents, nothing is required.
families.closest_grammar_spec: EVENTUALLY d UNTIL USER SAYS c
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Dwyer's 'before R' scope semantics, vacuous when R never occurs: EVENTUALLY d BEFORE USER SAYS c = (!c) W (d & !c) (x2, EQUIVALENT). Weak family: it differs from the covered EVENTUALLY d UNTIL c only on traces where c never occurs, which the generator never produces; contact-center-platforms-1's submitter reached the same conclusion. Distinct from F11 (e16).

families.name: Bounded gap (at least every k), starting at reply 1
families.schematic: d & G(d -> (N d | N N d | ... | N^k d)), d:A; k=3 (turn analogue); real-time version bounds the gap in hours
families.plain_meaning: Disclose in the first reply, and never let more than k replies (or k hours) pass without another disclosure; extra disclosures are allowed.
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Pattern AT LEAST EVERY k, a (Konrad-Cheng bounded recurrence) plus a non-exclusive IN REPLY n, a (checker: bare 'd at reply 1' is itself NOT COVERED, x3a, because AT 1 forbids d elsewhere). Real-time version needs a timestamped trace; the China CAC exact-period variant is covered by EVERY k in its turn analogue. Already a known near miss; new mass here is four binding laws (WA, GA, NY, and SB 243).

families.name: First and last reply
families.plain_meaning: The disclaimer must appear in the first reply and in the final reply of the conversation; replies in between are free.
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Two non-exclusive position patterns: IN REPLY n, a and IN THE LAST REPLY, a (both NOT COVERED alone: x3a, x3b). The member is their conjunction. Caveat kept from the submission: if 'end' is read as the agent's sign-off turn, it collapses to ALWAYS(!c | d), which is covered.

families.name: Order-free conditional existence
families.schematic: (F c) -> (F a), c:U or A (or a disjunction across sides), a:A; full rule is a conjunction over languages
families.plain_meaning: If the condition ever holds anywhere in the conversation, the action must appear in some reply, before or after the condition.
families.closest_grammar_spec: EVENTUALLY a FROM USER SAYS c (requires a after c)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Pattern IF EVER t THEN EVENTUALLY a (order-free). Checker on the one-condition skeleton (F c) -> (F a) with c:U: NOT COVERED (x4).
families.spec_class: PROPOSITIONAL (the general rule quantifies over the finite set of languages)

families.name: Cumulative non-completion (never all parts across the conversation)
families.schematic: !((F p) & (F q) & (F r)) = G !p | G !q | G !r, p,q,r:A; n components
families.plain_meaning: Each component may appear on its own, any number of times, but the conversation as a whole must never contain all n components.
families.closest_grammar_spec: NEVER p (too strict: forbids legitimate partial help)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Pattern NEVER ALL OF a1, ..., an (a disjunction of absences; conjunctions of grammar instances cannot express a disjunction). Distinct from F2's agent-guardrails-standards-5 (same side multiset, e17).

families.name: Assistant-toggled mode with a user event confined to it and an obligation to close
families.schematic: G((c -> Y((!r) S p)) & (p -> N(F r))), p:A, r:A, c:U
families.plain_meaning: The user's card data may arrive only while the assistant's most recent pause/resume action was a pause, and every pause must be followed by a resume later in the call.
families.closest_grammar_spec: FROM t UNTIL t' (user-side openers and closers, first segment only, constraining the assistant)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Repeated scope (F5) with assistant-side openers and closers (F1's ASSISTANT Act trigger), whose constrained event is user-side, plus a response pattern with an assistant trigger (r eventually after each p). Needs both extensions at once, so it does not collapse into F5 (which constrains A between U events).

families.name: Report the latest value given (overwrite semantics)
families.schematic: forall x: G(ic -> (s_x <-> ((!ao_x) S a_x))), ic:U, a_x:U, ao_x:U, s_x:A
families.plain_meaning: On every initial contact, the reply must state the most recently assigned altitude and no earlier one.
families.closest_grammar_spec: ALWAYS s_x FROM USER SAYS a_x (latches on the first assignment and ignores later amendments)
families.proposed_grammar_extension: Data binding on the user side: a pattern 'AT trig, STATE THE LATEST VALUE OF slot', which needs a value variable bound by the last u with a_x; per-value skeleton additionally needs past Since ('latest wins'), which no grammar pattern has.
families.spec_class: DATA (QUANTIFIED over altitude values; per-value skeleton not a grammar instance)

families.notes:
I put all 33 examples into 18 families, each example in exactly one. Two examples share a family when their formulas, or conjunctions of them, are instances of the same parametric schematic. The parameters are: atoms with their side (A or U) and possible negation, counts m and k, a one-step offset (Y or N, or none), and in F2 and F4 an optional release or invalidator literal. I confirmed exact equivalence with the checker wherever the schematic says two members are the same. Members of F2, F4 and F11 share a schematic but are not pairwise equivalent, and the checker confirmed this for F2 (e07).

Equivalence-mode results:
- EQUIVALENT:
  - e01: ai-law-3 and finance-identity-5 (F1).
  - e02: finance-identity-6 and agent-guardrails-standards-1 (F3).
  - e03: safety-critical-dialogue-2 and agent-guardrails-standards-6 (F5).
  - e04: finance-identity-2 equals (NEVER d UNTIL s) conjoined with the repeated hold G(i -> ((!d) W s)), so it goes in F5.
  - e06: safety-critical-dialogue-1 equals two instances of safety-critical-dialogue-5's skeleton (F10).
  - x1: ai-law-5 equals 'FROM the 2nd i' wrapped around the repeated hold.
  - x2: telecom-collections-2 equals Dwyer's existence-before-R.
  - x5: frontier-policies-3 equals NEVER c UNTIL (k OR 2nd w).
- NOT EQUIVALENT (these keep families apart where the atom sides match): e05, e07, e08, e09, e10, e11, e12, e13, e14, e15, e16, e17.
- Single-formula checks: bare 'd at reply 1' (x3a), 'd in the last reply' (x3b) and (F c) -> (F a) (x4) are all NOT COVERED. That is why F13 and F14 need non-exclusive position patterns.

Outputs are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mahyar-GitHub-temporal-if/abc04521-67a3-4e6c-a27a-e0348909db02/scratchpad/fam/ (e01.out to e17.out, x1.out to x5.out; the jobs are listed in jobs.tsv and jobs2.tsv).

Extensions that cover several families, which matters for choosing the smallest set of additions:
1. Assistant-side triggers. This means 'ASSISTANT Act' as a scope closer or opener, and 'USER SAYS p AFTER ASSISTANT Act', i.e. u & Y a. They alone cover F1 and F10. Together with the counting extensions they also serve F2, F3, F11 and F17. That touches about 18 of 33 examples, so this is the dominant gap.
2. Repeated scopes (FROM t UNTIL t' EACH TIME). Needed by F5, F6 and F17.
3. Counted or resettable triggers ('m-th time or later', 'm in a row', 'm-th since last r'). Needed by F6, F7, F8 and F9, and F2 needs a counted closer.

Classification flags:
- F12 is weak. Its only difference from the covered EVENTUALLY d UNTIL c is on traces where c never occurs, and the generator never produces those.
- F13 is the already-known at-least-every-k near miss. What is new is its binding-law instances.
- F5 is the known 'repeated mode toggles' near miss, now with federal-regulation and PSD2 instances.
- In finance-identity-2 and agent-guardrails-standards-6 the wall-clock timer is modeled as an injected U-side timeout event. Without that event they are REAL_TIME.
- QUANTIFIED DATA members, each placed by its per-value skeleton: telecom-collections-5, telecom-collections-6, finance-identity-3, frontier-policies-1, safety-critical-dialogue-5, agent-guardrails-standards-2 and safety-critical-dialogue-6.

The GA SB 540 PDF has the same clause (line 341) with AG enforcement. NY and China CAC add more jurisdictions. It also protects minors.

Utah statute on mental-health chatbots: fines up to $2,500 per violation, enforced by the Division of Consumer Protection. It covers users in distress.

I fetched the GA SB 540 text. It contains '(4) Escalation procedures for repeated or severe crisis indicators', AG civil actions and up to $10,000 per knowing violation. It concerns crisis and minors' safety, and the teen-suicide lawsuits show real failures.

The crisis domain is safety-critical, but CA AB 1988 was never enacted (its Senate hearing was canceled). It is a concrete legislative proposal that binds nobody. I demoted it below binding rules but kept it above best-practice guides.
FTC TSR 16 CFR 310.4(d) is binding on every telemarketer, including AI voice agents. It carries FTC and state AG civil penalties and has a long enforcement history.
FTC TSR 310.3(a)(1), a binding deceptive-practice rule with civil penalties.
CFPB Reg F 1006.18(e)(4) under the FDCPA: statutory damages and class-action exposure, and debt collection is a regulated industry.
FTC TSR 310.3(a)(3) express verifiable authorization. Binding, and it governs the actual movement of consumer money.
FTC TSR 310.4(d) upsell seller-identity disclosure. Binding, with civil penalties.
Mandatory network policy for all 988 Lifeline crisis centers. It is safety-critical: imminent suicide risk, and involuntary emergency interventions.
PSD2 RTS (Reg. 2018/389) Art. 4(3)(b) binds every EU PSP and is enforced by national competent authorities. It is a security control against credential brute-forcing.

PCI SSC information supplement: payment-card compliance guidance under contractually mandated PCI DSS. It names both failure modes. It is regulated-industry compliance but not itself a law with penalties.
SEC Rule 17a-14 (Form CRS) binds broker-dealers and is an exam and enforcement item.
Safety mitigation in the deployed OpenAI ChatGPT agent, at large scale. Violations are measured: about 91% confirmation recall, so about 9% misses on financial transactions.
PSD2 RTS Art. 4(3)(d) 5-minute inactivity limit, binding on EU PSPs.
PSD2 RTS Art. 5 dynamic linking plus Art. 4(1) single use. Binding, and it defends against manipulated payments.

final.disagreements:
Only one disagreement crossed the threshold. No example differed by 2 or more tiers. The largest example gap was ai-law-5 (3 vs 4), and the largest family-rank gap was F12 (12 vs 9).

F12 (rank 12 vs 9, a gap of 3). I fetched the FTC TSR compliance guide. It confirms the quote ('must give a consumer the information required by Section 310.3(a)(1) of the TSR before: Getting a consumer's consent to buy') and a civil penalty of $53,088 per violation. It cites no specific enforcement actions. Ranker 1 moved F12 down because the family is formally weak and because the telemarketing domain already appears in F1 and F2. Neither reason is in the rubric: domains are counted within a family, not across families. F12 therefore ties the other single-member, single-domain tier-5 families (F9, F15, F14), none of which has documented violations, and the decision falls to scale. I placed F12 at 10, right after F9. Both rules bind an entire national or EU market. PSD2 covers every EU payment account and guards against account takeover. F12 is above F15 (narrower AI collections deployment) and F14 (California audio-only health communications). The formal-weakness note on F12 belongs in the spec-selection decision, not in its importance rank.

Below-threshold differences I settled in passing:
- ai-law-5: tier 3. It is an unenacted bill, so it does not count as compliance in a deployed system. F6 stays at 17 either way.
- F14 vs F15: F15 at 11 and F14 at 12, because F14 has the narrowest scope.
- F9: rank 9, between the two rankers' 9 and 10.

Ranks 1-8 and 13-18 were the same in both rankings, including F4 above F10 on the documented-violations tiebreak.
